Estimate ion-rarity weights from a spectral library

Source: R/ion_weights.R
library_ion_weights.Rd

Compute reusable smoothed inverse-document-frequency weights from reference spectra. Rare ions receive larger weights than ubiquitous fragments.

Usage

library_ion_weights(
  library,
  mass = 33:550,
  min_relative = 0.01,
  power = 1,
  ncores = NULL,
  batch_size = 4096L
)

Arguments

library

A GCMSlibrary.

mass

Acquired nominal mass bins; default 33:550.

min_relative

An ion is present when its intensity is positive and at least this fraction of the acquired-bin base peak, default 0.01.

power

Exponent for inverse-frequency weighting, default 1. Zero gives uniform weights; larger values put more emphasis on rare ions.

ncores

Native worker count; NULL uses physical cores.

batch_size

Number of library spectra read per batch.

Value

A named numeric vector of weights, normalized to mean one. Attributes frequency, spectra, min_relative, power and seconds record its derivation.

Details

If L nonempty reference spectra are available and d_j contain ion j, weights are proportional to [1+log((L+1)/(d_j+1))]^power. Frequencies are counted across reference spectra, using the requested acquisition bins. Zero-intensity spectra are omitted. Nominal duplicates are summed before applying the relative threshold. Source intensities and totals are preserved.

Build weights once and reuse them in library_search(ion_weights=...). SQLite records are read in bounded batches; native frequency counts use OpenMP. For validation, estimate weights from the reference catalogue after excluding query records and near-duplicates. Uniform weights remain the search default.

See also

[library_search()]

Examples

f <- tempfile(fileext=".msp")
writeLines(c("Name: A", "Num Peaks: 2", "43 100;57 20;",
             "Name: B", "Num Peaks: 2", "43 100;91 50;"), f)
lib <- read_msp(f)
w <- library_ion_weights(lib, mass=c(43,57,91), ncores=1)
w
